Playbook.name: O365 — MFA Fatigue: Repeated MFA Challenges Rejected/Ignored for One User - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Credential Access / Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: One account received >=5 MFA-interrupt failures (UserStrongAuthClientAuthNRequiredInterrupt) in the window - the MFA-fatigue / push-bombing pattern where an attacker with a valid password spams MFA prompts hoping the user approves. Triage: a real fatigue attack (password already known), or a broken client re-prompting?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: MFA fatigue means the attacker already has the password and only needs one accidental approval to fully compromise the account.

Assets.AssetType: Exchange Online, SharePoint/OneDrive, Teams, Entra directory

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: O365 unified audit via Elastic Agent (verified live). Fields: event.action, user.name, source.ip, o365.audit.Operation, o365.audit.ResultStatus, o365.audit.ObjectId, o365.audit.ModifiedProperties, o365.audit.Parameters, o365.audit.UserId. INGEST LAG 20-60 min - all queries use a 4h window and timestamp_override event.ingested at rule level.
JCB egress NAT is 94.249.88.0/24 - internal users appear from it.

Signal.Name: MFA Fatigue: Repeated MFA Challenges Rej

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the repeated MFA challenges are an attacker push-bombing (password known) or a client fault.

Step.name: MFA-interrupt pattern and source
Step.Purpose: Repeated interrupts from an unusual source with a known-good password is push-bombing; a single client re-prompting differs.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE event.dataset == "o365.audit" AND event.action == "UserLoginFailed" AND user.name == "$username" AND o365.audit.LogonError == "UserStrongAuthClientAuthNRequiredInterrupt" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS interrupts = COUNT(*), sources = VALUES(source.ip), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Many interrupts from a foreign/unusual source = push-bombing (attacker has the password). A single internal source may be a broken client. Note whether the source is the egress NAT (internal) or external.

Step.name: Did a successful login follow (fatigue succeeded)
Step.Purpose: A UserLoggedIn after the interrupt burst means the user approved - full compromise.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE event.dataset == "o365.audit" AND user.name == "$username" AND event.action == "UserLoggedIn" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS logins = COUNT(*), sources = VALUES(source.ip), first_success = MIN(@timestamp) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: A success from the same unusual source after the interrupts = the user approved a malicious prompt - IR immediately.

Node.Condition: Interrupt burst from an external source followed by a successful login (user approved).
Node.Result: True Positive (MFA Fatigue Succeeded - IR, reset + revoke)

Node.Condition: Interrupt burst from an external source, no success yet.
Node.Result: True Positive (MFA Fatigue Attack in Progress - escalate, protect account)

Node.Condition: Interrupts from a single internal client (broken re-prompt loop).

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-O365MFA-PATTERN, INV-02-O365MFA-SUCCESS to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A benign client re-prompting for MFA.

Indicators.Item: No success from an unusual source.

SOCAction.Item: Fix the client; close as misconfiguration/false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: An MFA push-bombing attack (password already compromised).

Indicators.Item: Interrupt burst from an external source.

SOCAction.Item: Reset the account + revoke tokens; block the source; the password is compromised - force change; enable number-matching MFA.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured client stuck re-requesting MFA.

SOCAction.Item: Fix the client MFA config; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the change/actor in the audit log.
If unexpected/unauthorised, disable the actor session and reverse the change.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Reverse the change; revoke sessions/tokens for the actor and affected principals.
Review the actor's other recent audit activity.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce MFA/conditional access; tighten admin consent and privileged-role governance (PIM); alert on these operations.

QualityChecks.Check: Account for O365 ingest lag (20-60 min) - short windows miss events; this rule uses event.ingested override.
Exclude the egress NAT 94.249.88.0/24 where source is used; tune known admin/automation via exceptions.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Account reset + tokens revoked; source blocked; number-matching enforced.
